chunks.text: Here's the equation for computing the Sharpe ratio as proposed by William Sharpe

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: himself. It's the expected value of the return on the portfolio minus the risk

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: free rate of return, divided by the standard deviation of that same difference.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: This is the x-ante formulation, meaning, you know, because we're using expected,

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: it's a forward looking measure of what the Sharpe ratio should be.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: Now to calculate this in reality, we need to look back at those values.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: So to calculate this in Python using historical data,

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: we just take the mean of daily returns minus the daily risk free rate and

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: divide that by the standard deviation of the daily returns minus the daily risk free rate.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: Now you may be wondering, what is this risk free rate?

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: Now, I've been presenting this as if this risk free rate changes each day.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: And indeed LIBOR changes each day and three month T-Bell changes a little bit each day.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: But there's a shortcut people use a lot that simplifies this equation significantly.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: And this shortcut makes sense because usually the risk free rate is not given on a daily basis for,

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: for instance, putting your money in a bank account or a certificate of deposit.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: Usually that's a percentage on an annual basis or a six month basis.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: So you can convert that annual amount into a daily amount using this simple trick.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: That means if we start at the beginning of the year with a value of 1.0,

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: at the end of the year we have 1.1.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: So we add 1 here.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: So this is the total value of our asset at the end of the year.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: Now what is the interest rate per day that would enable us to get to this value?

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: It's a number that if we multiply it by itself each day for each day in the trading

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: year or 252 times would arrive at this number.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
chunks.text: So here's how we do it.

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio

chunks.title: Computing sharpe ratio
